title: FLOP Network health — flop-watch
description: Independent, read-only observability for FLOP Network Devnet and Testnet.

options.content: Independent, read-only monitor of FLOP Network Devnet and Testnet, from a single vantage point. Not affiliated with FLOP Labs. **Measured**: observed by flop-watch. **Reported**: stated by a FLOP node or service. **Derived**: computed by a rule from other signals. **Self**: about flop-watch itself. Times are UTC. Source and method: [github.com/tarikcaykara/flop-watch](https://github.com/tarikcaykara/flop-watch).

panels.title: RPC WebSocket
panels.description: Measured · `system_health` over flop-watch's RPC WebSocket, every 30 s. Down means the last attempt failed: the health call, the connection, or the setup after connecting.

panels.title: RPC HTTP
panels.description: Measured · `chain_getHeader` and `system_health` over HTTP JSON-RPC, every 30 s. Down means at least one of the two failed in the last cycle.

panels.title: Best head age
panels.description: Derived · time since flop-watch received the last new-head notification over the WebSocket. Blocks come every second, so over 30 s means no new block reached us.

panels.title: Finality lag
panels.description: Derived · best minus finalized block number, from the WebSocket subscriptions. 30 and 120 blocks are the yellowpaper's warning and freeze thresholds.

panels.title: Faucet claims
panels.description: Derived · mirrors the Testnet faucet page's check (research §7): `/chain` and `/limits` fetched, the faucet's genesis matches, `stale` is false and the status is `open`. Not checked: the network names, which the genesis check covers, and the page's agent-lane constants. The page itself checks only on load, so it can stay disabled after this recovers.

panels.title: Faucet status
panels.description: Reported · `faucet.status` from the faucet's `/limits`, every 60 s.

panels.title: Explorer
panels.description: Measured · GET `/api/stats` on the explorer, every 60 s. Down means the request failed or did not return a JSON object.

panels.title: Genesis
panels.description: Reported · the genesis hash from the RPC WebSocket, RPC HTTP and the faucet, against the pinned one. A mismatch points to a network reset or an endpoint serving another chain; the Identity row shows which source.

panels.title: Incidents
panels.description: Derived · Prometheus alert rules over flop-watch's signals. Each alert's category (measured, reported, derived) is in the Firing now table.

targets.expr:
3 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="critical", network=~"$network|"})
or 2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="warning", network=~"$network|"})
or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="info", network=~"$network|"})
or on() label_replace(vector(0), "alertname", "No incident", "", "")

panels.title: Firing now
panels.description: Derived · the alerts firing now, with the category of the signal each one reads.

panels.title: Last successful probe
panels.description: Measured · when each probe last succeeded. A target missing here has not succeeded since the collector started.

panels.title: RPC availability
panels.description: Measured · flop-watch's WebSocket connection and its 30 s probes over the WebSocket and HTTP. Gaps mean the collector was not running or Prometheus could not scrape it.

panels.title: RPC latency
panels.description: Measured · response time of the RPC probes from one vantage point, including our network path and the Cloudflare edge. HTTP includes the genesis check every 10 min.

panels.title: RPC failures
panels.description: Measured · failed RPC requests by result: timeout, network error, HTTP error, JSON-RPC error, invalid response or rate limited.

panels.title: WebSocket reconnects
panels.description: Measured · WebSocket connections opened, and closed by reason: a remote close, an error, or flop-watch's stall watchdog (no new head for 30 s).

panels.title: Node peers and syncing
panels.description: Reported · peers and the syncing flag from `system_health`, of whichever RPC node behind the load balancer answered. This describes that node, not the network.

panels.title: Heads now
panels.description: Reported · the latest block numbers from the WebSocket subscriptions, `chain_getHeader` over HTTP and the explorer's `/api/stats`.

panels.title: Finality lag
panels.description: Derived · best minus finalized block number. 30 and 120 blocks are the yellowpaper's warning and freeze thresholds. Devnet can go negative, probably because its WebSocket streams come from more than one backend.

panels.title: Head age
panels.description: Derived · time since the last new-head and finalized-head notifications reached flop-watch. This reflects delivery to us, not block production.

panels.title: Block interval
panels.description: Reported · BABE slot delta times slot duration, between consecutive, parent-linked blocks. 1 s is normal; anything higher means empty slots.

panels.title: Skipped and rewound heads
panels.description: Measured · blocks the new-head subscription skipped, and notifications at or below the previous height. Skips are about delivery to us; rewinds can also come from short forks.

panels.title: Claims ready
panels.description: Derived · mirrors the Testnet faucet page's check (research §7): `/chain` and `/limits` fetched, the faucet's genesis matches, `stale` is false and the status is `open`. Not checked: the network names, which the genesis check covers, and the page's agent-lane constants. The page itself checks only on load, so it can stay disabled after this recovers.

panels.title: Faucet probes
panels.description: Measured · GET `/limits`, `/health` and `/chain` every 60 s. `/health` counts as up on its 503 'degraded' answer too, because that is a valid answer; `/chain` counts as up only with a valid genesis hash.

panels.title: Status
panels.description: Reported · `faucet.status` and `stale` from `/limits`.

panels.title: Sponsor lanes
panels.description: Reported · `sponsor.miner.status` and `sponsor.validator.status` from `/limits`. The official page shows 'Unavailable' for both when its own check fails.

targets.expr:
sum by (lane) (flopwatch_faucet_sponsor_status{network="$network", status="open"})
+ 2 * sum by (lane) (flopwatch_faucet_sponsor_status{network="$network", status="automatic_full"})
+ 3 * sum by (lane) (flopwatch_faucet_sponsor_status{network="$network", status="positions_full"})
+ 4 * sum by (lane) (flopwatch_faucet_sponsor_status{network="$network", status="unknown"})
+ 5 * sum by (lane) (flopwatch_faucet_sponsor_status{network="$network", status="other"})

panels.title: Balance
panels.description: Reported · the faucet's balance and its minimum balance, from `/limits`.

panels.title: Daily cap
panels.description: Reported · the faucet's daily cap: used, limit and remaining, from `/limits`.

panels.title: Pending grants
panels.description: Reported · `faucet.pendingGrants` from `/limits`. A rising count means grants are queued and not yet paid out.

panels.title: /health
panels.description: Measured (HTTP status) and reported (ready) · GET `/health`. The faucet scopes `ready` to the client asking, here flop-watch's own address, so it is not global claim readiness; see Claims ready.

panels.title: Dependencies
panels.description: Reported · `dependencies.<name>.ok` from `/health`. A dependency without an `ok` field, such as `signing`, has no row.

panels.title: Indexer lag (faucet)
panels.description: Reported · `dependencies.indexer.details.lagBlocks` from `/health`: how far the faucet's indexer is behind its chain head.

panels.title: /limits data age
panels.description: Derived · time since the `asOf` of the last `/limits` answer. It swings between about 0.4 and 5.4 min in normal operation; the alert fires only when it stays over 5 min for 5 min.

panels.title: Response time
panels.description: Measured · p95 response time of the faucet probes from one vantage point.

panels.title: Explorer probe
panels.description: Measured · GET `/api/stats` every 60 s, best effort, because the API is undocumented.

panels.title: Indexer lag (explorer)
panels.description: Derived · our best block minus the explorer's latest indexed block. It can be slightly negative, because the two sources are read at different moments and may come from different nodes.

panels.title: Finality view (explorer)
panels.description: Reported · the explorer's own finality lag and `safeMode` flag from `/api/stats`. The explorer reports its own thresholds as 30 (warn) and 120 (freeze) blocks.

panels.title: Chain identity
panels.description: Reported · `system_chain`, `state_getRuntimeVersion` and `chain_getBlockHash [0]` over the WebSocket, read on every connect.

panels.title: Genesis match
panels.description: Reported · whether each source's genesis hash equals the pinned one: the RPC WebSocket, RPC HTTP (every 10 min) and the faucet's `/chain` (every 60 s).

panels.title: Runtime version
panels.description: Reported · the runtime `specVersion` from the runtime-version subscription. Each step is a runtime upgrade, also marked as an annotation.

panels.title: Slot duration
panels.description: Reported · BABE slot duration from `BabeApi_configuration`.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Self · the running flop-watch version.

panels.title: Requests to FLOP
panels.description: Self · flop-watch's steady-state requests to this network's endpoints, against the 0.25 requests/s budget: every probe request, including the WebSocket health pings. Reconnect identity calls and subscriptions are not counted.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Self · the collector's resident memory. The MVP target is under 150 MB.

panels.title: Schema mismatches
panels.description: Self · remote fields that were missing or had an unexpected type in the selected time range. A FLOP service probably changed its JSON.
